name: Eiffel Tower
description: Built for the 1889 Paris World’s Fair, this iron tower grew from an ambitious engineering project into a symbol of France. Its open lattice structure was assembled from more than 18,000 metal parts.

name: Colosseum
description: The Flavian emperors built this vast amphitheatre in the first century CE. Crowds gathered here for gladiator contests and animal hunts, making it a major venue for public spectacles in ancient Rome.

name: Stonehenge
description: Raised in prehistoric times, these enormous stones form a circle in the Wiltshire landscape. Together with nearby ancient sites, they offer clues to the beliefs and astronomical knowledge of the people who built them.

name: Statue of Liberty
description: France gave this monument to the United States, and it was dedicated in 1886. Standing at the entrance to New York Harbor, it became a symbol of liberty and a familiar sight for arriving immigrants.

name: Sydney Opera House
description: Opened in 1973, this performing arts landmark was designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon. Its overlapping shell-shaped roofs turn the edge of Sydney Harbour into a striking architectural silhouette.

name: Mount Fuji
description: This 3,776-metre volcano has inspired pilgrims, poets and artists for centuries. Its often snow-covered summit appears in celebrated Japanese woodblock prints, while shrines and pilgrimage routes connect the mountain to living traditions.

name: Taj Mahal
description: Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned this white-marble mausoleum in the seventeenth century in memory of Mumtaz Mahal. Its carefully balanced buildings and gardens stand beside the Yamuna River and reflect the craft of Mughal architecture.

name: Petra
description: The Nabataeans made Petra a crossroads for caravan trade. Buildings carved into rock sit among mountains and narrow gorges, combining local traditions with architectural influences from the Hellenistic world.

name: Chichén Itzá
description: This ancient Maya city preserves temples and monuments shaped by both Maya traditions and influences from central Mexico. El Castillo and the round observatory El Caracol are among its best-known surviving buildings.

name: Angkor Wat
description: Built in the twelfth century under King Suryavarman II, Angkor Wat began as a temple devoted to Vishnu and later became a Buddhist sacred site. Its carved galleries tell religious stories and record scenes from the Khmer kingdom.

name: Machu Picchu
description: The Inca built this mountain settlement about 2,430 metres above sea level. Stone walls, terraces and ramps follow the steep terrain, linking remarkable engineering with the surrounding mountain forest.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza
description: Built as the tomb of King Khufu, the Great Pyramid once had a smooth outer covering of fine limestone. It is the only surviving wonder of the ancient world’s traditional Seven Wonders.
descriptionSourceName: Egypt Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
description: Founded in 1395, Gyeongbokgung was the principal palace of the Joseon dynasty. Its halls and courtyards stand below Bugaksan; after destruction in the sixteenth century, the palace was rebuilt in the nineteenth century.

name: Merlion
description: With a lion’s head and a fish’s body, the Merlion brings together two images of Singapore. The original waterfront statue was unveiled in 1972 and became a familiar symbol of the city.

name: Brandenburg Gate
description: Built between 1788 and 1791, this sandstone gate brought Greek-inspired architecture to Berlin. A four-horse chariot crowns its columns, and the gate became closely associated with Germany’s division and reunification.

name: Belém Tower
description: This fortified tower stands beside the Tagus at the entrance to Lisbon’s harbour. Its carved stonework and corner turrets recall the maritime world of sixteenth-century Portugal.

name: Christ the Redeemer
description: Unveiled in 1931, this Art Deco statue stands on Corcovado above Rio de Janeiro. Its outstretched arms form a distinctive silhouette over the city’s forested hills and coastline.

name: Burj Khalifa
description: Opened in 2010, the 828-metre Burj Khalifa rises above central Dubai. Its tapering profile steps upward to a slender spire, while observation decks offer views across the city and desert.

name: Hagia Sophia
description: A landmark of sixth-century Istanbul, Hagia Sophia is celebrated for its vast dome and the space beneath it. It forms part of the city’s historic areas, where centuries of religious and architectural traditions meet.

name: Borobudur Temple
description: Built in the eighth and ninth centuries, this Buddhist temple rises through square terraces and circular platforms to a central stupa. Carved reliefs and smaller stupas turn the ascent into a journey through stone.

name: Great Zimbabwe
description: The stone ruins of Great Zimbabwe preserve a major Shona centre that flourished between the eleventh and fifteenth centuries. Its great enclosures and conical tower recall a city connected to long-distance trade.

name: Sagrada Família
description: Antoni Gaudí made nature a guide for this Barcelona basilica. Branching columns distribute the building’s weight like a stone forest, while geometric forms and coloured light shape its distinctive interior.

name: Moai of Rapa Nui
description: The people of Rapa Nui developed a remarkable tradition of monumental stone sculpture. These large human figures, known as moai, stand within a Polynesian cultural landscape of ceremonial sites on the remote Pacific island.

name: Great Wall of China
description: Successive dynasties built and linked fortifications across northern China, with construction continuing into the Ming period. Walls, watchtowers and mountain passes form an immense defensive landscape shaped by centuries of work.

name: CN Tower
description: Opened in 1976, Toronto’s communications and observation tower rises about 553 metres. A broad observation pod wraps around its slender concrete shaft beneath a long antenna.

name: Kinderdijk Windmills
description: Windmills, dykes and waterways at Kinderdijk tell the story of keeping low-lying land dry. The mill network belongs to a water-management landscape shaped over centuries for settlement and farming.

name: Hallgrímskirkja
description: Consecrated in 1986, this Reykjavík church was designed by Guðjón Samúelsson. Its rising concrete forms echo Iceland’s columnar rock, mountains and glaciers, gathering around a tall central tower.

name: Atomium
description: Built for the 1958 Brussels World’s Fair, the Atomium turns an iron crystal’s unit cell into architecture. Nine metallic spheres are joined by tubes, giving the structure its unmistakable geometric silhouette.

name: Petronas Twin Towers
description: Designed by César Pelli, these paired towers rise 451.9 metres above Kuala Lumpur. Their stepped profiles and slender spires frame a skybridge linking the two 88-storey buildings.

name: Shwedagon Pagoda
description: On Singuttara Hill in Yangon, Shwedagon is a major Buddhist pilgrimage site. Its gold-covered central stupa rises above terraces, shrines and pavilions, crowned by a jewelled umbrella.

name: Acropolis of Athens
description: Above Athens, this rocky hill preserves an ensemble of ancient Greek monuments. Major buildings from the fifth century BCE include the Parthenon, the Propylaea and the Erechtheion.

name: Saint Basil’s Cathedral
description: Built between 1555 and 1561, this cathedral stands on Moscow’s Red Square. Its clustered chapels and varied onion-shaped domes create a distinctive skyline whose appearance evolved over later centuries.

name: Ait-Ben-Haddou
description: This fortified settlement near Ouarzazate groups earthen buildings behind defensive walls and corner towers. Its compact hillside forms exemplify the traditional architecture of Morocco’s pre-Saharan region.

name: Sigiriya
description: A granite rock rises roughly 180 metres above the surrounding landscape at Sigiriya. The ruins of King Kassapa I’s fifth-century capital occupy its summit, approached by galleries and stairways through a monumental lion entrance.

name: Sossusvlei
description: Deep orange dunes surround a pale salt-and-clay pan in the Namib Desert. Sossusvlei formed where sand blocked the Tsauchab River; after exceptional rains, water can reach this usually dry basin.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description: At 5,895 metres, Kilimanjaro is Africa’s highest mountain. Its volcanic massif rises above the surrounding plains, with forested slopes and a snow-covered summit forming a striking sequence of landscapes.

name: Prague Astronomical Clock
description: Mounted on Prague’s Old Town Hall, this astronomical clock combines timekeeping with a calendar and zodiac display. Its decorated dials and figures turn the tower wall into a miniature theatre of the sky.

name: Hungarian Parliament Building
description: This monumental home of Hungary’s National Assembly combines a richly detailed Neo-Gothic exterior with a prominent central dome. Rows of pointed windows and slender pinnacles give the long building its distinctive skyline.

name: Schönbrunn Palace
description: Schönbrunn developed from a hunting estate into the Habsburgs’ summer residence. Its broad yellow palace fronts an extensive garden landscape, bringing court architecture and formal outdoor spaces together.

name: Matterhorn
description: The sharply angled Matterhorn rises above Zermatt on the border between Switzerland and Italy. Its steep rock faces and snowy ridges make a striking pyramid-shaped outline in the Alpine landscape.

name: The Little Mermaid
description: Edvard Eriksen’s bronze sculpture has sat beside Copenhagen’s Langelinie waterfront since 1913. Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen’s tale, the small figure on a rock became an enduring symbol of the city.

name: Borgund Stave Church
description: Borgund preserves a distinctive example of Norway’s medieval timber churches. Stacked roofs, carved dragon heads and elaborate portals rise above wooden galleries, showing the craft of stave construction.

name: Helsinki Cathedral
description: Consecrated in 1852, Helsinki Cathedral is a central part of the city’s neoclassical monumental centre. Its columned portico, broad steps and domes create a recognisable silhouette above Senate Square.

name: Obelisk of Buenos Aires
description: Built in 1936 to mark four centuries since the city’s first foundation, the Obelisco stands where Avenida Corrientes meets Avenida 9 de Julio. Its slender shaft and pointed crown make it a familiar Buenos Aires landmark.

name: Walls of Dubrovnik
description: Stone walls and defensive towers surround Dubrovnik’s historic centre beside the Adriatic. Inside, churches, palaces and fountains recall the city’s long life as an important Mediterranean maritime power.

name: Boudhanath Stupa
description: Boudhanath is one of the Buddhist monument groups within the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage property. A great white dome supports a gilded tower marked with Buddha’s eyes, giving the stupa its powerful, simple form.

name: Ha Long Bay
description: Limestone islands and steep green towers rise from the waters of Ha Long Bay in northeastern Vietnam. Part of the Ha Long Bay–Cat Ba Archipelago World Heritage property, the seascape reveals karst shaped over a long geological history.

name: Hegra
description: At Hegra, Nabataean builders cut monumental tombs directly into sandstone outcrops. Decorated facades, inscriptions and wells preserve traces of a caravan city and its skilful use of the desert landscape.
